test.name: Thin subject: a clean-looking hit is reported as needs-review, never as the subject
test.description: The subject (William Brown, b. 1872 Virginia) has no date narrower than a year and no named spouse, parent or child, so record_search's ranked carries subjectTooThin: true. The single 1900 hit agrees with everything the tree holds and ranks 0.94, and nothing in the project separates him from a namesake. The reply must present the hit as needs-review, report none of its family as the subject's, and name the anchor and the record likely to state it. Extraction is not graded. Issue #2213 d29.

judge_context: CORE: `ranked.subjectTooThin` is true on the search response — the tree holds only a birth year and no relatives, so nothing separates this William Brown from any other William Brown in Bedford County. The hit must be presented as needs-review, whatever its matchScore. Extraction is not graded: it records what the record says and claims no identity.

Score Result triage 1 if the reply calls the hit a confirmed match, 'our William', 'almost certainly him', or otherwise presents it as clearing identity, or reports a relative from the record as the subject's. A high score on a too-thin subject measures only that nothing disagrees, not that anything agrees.

Score Completeness 3 when the hit is reported and flagged needs-review, the search is logged, and the reply names what would confirm identity (e.g. a named spouse, child or parent, or a more precise birth date) and the record most likely to state it. Wording is free.

The census `wiki_read` from Step 2's pre-work block is NOT graded on Tool Arguments — score that dimension on the `record_search` call's arguments. The census fixture's predicate matches any URL containing `United_States_Census`, so a per-year page is answered by the same country page; that is the shape of the fixture set, not a wrong call.
